newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya expects rise in sugar output to 462,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Kenya expects rise in sugar output to 462,000 T.

text.p: Kenya's sugar production will rise to 462,000 tonnes this calendar year and then further grow to 485,000 tonnes in 1998 compared with 420,000 tonnes in 1996, senior sugar authorities forecast on Wednesday.

"It is assumed that the weather conditions shall be favourable -- that there will be adequate rainfall and we therefore shall not experience drought," said Kenya Sugar Authority (KSA) Chief Executive Francis Chahonyo.
The production estimates compare with consumption that has remained stagnant at 560,000 tonnes in the last two years.
Chahonyo and a number of senior government officials had complained previously that efforts at encouraging sugar production were hampered by a flood of imports on the market.

They say the imports cost less, primarily because traders brought it in without paying mandatory anti-dumping taxes. Last year, Chahonyo demanded action from the customs department to stem the imports.
Most of the imports are marked under transit but end up on the local market.
Kenya has six major white sugar millers and a seventh that produces only 500 tonnes per year, according to official statistics.
